authorityPolicy: Recommendations are proposals, not decisions. Original registers remain authoritative pending explicit migration.

questions.question: Can a board-delegated, version-pinned policy be the sponsor's approval of each routine grant?
questions.blocks: DD-004 routine path; headcount model; TVCTL-09
questions.optionsOrValidation: Yes with conditions · batch human approval · per-grant human

decision.recommendedAnswer: Working design: conditional, board-delegated, version-pinned policy approval for routine grants, only if sponsor counsel confirms legality and the sponsor board formally authorizes a bounded policy and delegation. Until then use an authorized human approval route; do not treat policy evaluation as sponsor approval.

validation.evidence: Required: written counsel opinion on applicable sponsor/grant law; sponsor board resolution defining delegation, eligible grants, exclusions, monetary limits, version pinning, independent policy publication, revocation and oversight; per-grant decision evidence linking policy version and delegation; independent assurance testing.

reviewHistory.note: User selected conditional policy-based approval as the proposed design, explicitly subject to counsel and sponsor board approval. This is not a legal conclusion or formal sponsor authorization.

questions.question: Which sanctions false-positive classes may a deterministic rule clear?
questions.optionsOrValidation: None · enumerated classes with QA sampling

decision.recommendedAnswer: Working design: permit deterministic clearing only for explicitly enumerated and version-controlled false-positive classes approved by compliance and counsel, supported by verifiable identity evidence, independent QA sampling, audit records, revocation controls and mandatory human escalation for all ambiguous or non-enumerated matches. AI models may identify or flag possible matches but must not independently clear sanctions holds.

validation.evidence: Required: CRCO and counsel approval of specific false-positive classes and rule predicates; current sanctions screening obligations and source applicability; negative and adversarial test sets; false-clear rate and independent QA thresholds; evidence retention, rule-change approval and emergency suspension design.

reviewHistory.note: User selected bounded deterministic clearing of enumerated sanctions false-positive classes, subject to compliance and legal review; no approval of actual classes or rules yet.

questions.question: On donor or sole-advisor death, what happens to sponsor-approved, unpaid grants?

decision.recommendedAnswer: Working design: donor or sole-advisor death does not automatically cancel sponsor-approved unpaid grants; proceed with previously authorized grants only if still valid and free of legal, compliance, funding, sanctions or payment holds. Suspend standing recommendations and new advisory instructions pending verification of death, effective authority, successor arrangements and sponsor review. Recheck material changes and preserve sponsor discretion under governing documents.

validation.evidence: Required: sponsor board and counsel approval; review of governing documents, applicable succession law and donor-advisor authority; definition of effective death notice, standing instruction suspension, post-approval changes and permissible holds; audit evidence of authority rechecks.

reviewHistory.note: User chose continuation of sponsor-approved unpaid grants after donor or sole-advisor death, subject to legal and compliance holds; suspend standing and future recommendations pending authority review. Sponsor board and counsel approval remain outstanding.

questions.question: Provisional credit limit for reversible contributions, and acknowledgment timing

decision.recommendedAnswer: Working design: use risk-based provisional credit limits for reversible contributions, defaulting to zero for new donors. Approved donor-specific limits must be bounded, documented, monitored and revocable, with exposure controls for returns, fraud, concentration and outstanding grant commitments. Model contribution receipt, sponsor gift acceptance, and grant-funding availability as distinct events and states; receipt or provisional posting alone does not establish irrevocable funds or permission to fund grants. Charitable acknowledgment issuance and tax-effective timing require counsel review and must not be inferred from grant-funding availability.

validation.evidence: Required: CFO-approved risk appetite, donor limit criteria, aggregate exposure caps, limit review/revocation process and reconciliation controls; legal counsel opinion on gift acceptance and charitable acknowledgment timing by contribution method and year-end edge cases; pilot return/fraud data and negative tests for post-grant reversal, partial return, insufficient liquidity and fraudulent funding.

reviewHistory.note: User selected risk-based provisional contribution credit, default zero for new donors and approved donor-specific limits; distinct receipt, gift acceptance and grant-funding availability; acknowledgment timing reserved for counsel review. Not a formal CFO or counsel approval.

questions.question: Valuation haircut rates by asset class for reservable capacity

decision.recommendedAnswer: Working design: govern reservable-capacity valuation through approved asset-class baseline haircuts, with bounded and explainable adjustments for volatility, market liquidity, portfolio concentration, stale or unreliable prices, and expected liquidation timing. CFO and Investment Committee approve the methodology, thresholds, exceptions and revisions. Back-test against historical drawdowns and liquidation outcomes, stress-test correlated market/liquidity shocks, and apply conservative capacity treatment when inputs are missing or stale. No arbitrary numerical haircut percentages are approved by this decision.

validation.evidence: Required: CFO and Investment Committee approval; asset-class risk taxonomy, approved data sources and price-age limits; historical drawdown and liquidation back-tests; correlated stress tests and scenario thresholds; model monitoring, overrides, independent challenge and change-control procedures; reconciliation against custodian holdings and available cash. Numerical rates remain open.

reviewHistory.note: User selected governed risk-sensitive valuation haircuts with approved asset-class baselines, volatility/liquidity/concentration/stale-price/liquidation adjustments, CFO and Investment Committee approval, back-testing and stress testing. No rates or formal approvals established.

questions.question: Is reservation atomic with approval?

decision.recommendedAnswer: Working design: routine grant approval and reservable-capacity encumbrance are one atomic, concurrency-safe operation; if either fails, neither takes effect and no approval or funding claim is communicated. For large or exceptional grants, a separately authorized internal decision may enter an explicit 'approved pending funding' state without reserved capacity, but must not be represented as funded, released, payable or externally committed. External commitments and recipient notifications are gated on applicable funding, accounting, legal, sponsor-authority and compliance conditions. State transitions, reservation ordering, expirations, rechecks and exception approval must be auditable.

validation.evidence: Required: CFO and product-owner approval; legal and accounting review of when an internal approval becomes an enforceable promise or recognized grant; sponsor delegation-of-authority and exception limits; concurrency and idempotency design; documented notification gates; testing for simultaneous approvals, stale valuations, partial failures, retries, reversals and reservation expiry.

reviewHistory.note: User selected atomic approval and reservation for routine grants; separate authorized pending-funding state for large/exceptional grants; prohibit external commitments until funding and legal conditions are satisfied. Formal approvals and legal/accounting review pending.

questions.question: When is a percentage grant fixed?

decision.recommendedAnswer: Working design: for ordinary percentage-based grants, calculate and fix the dollar amount at sponsor approval using a documented, time-stamped valuation snapshot, fund scope, percentage, applicable available-capacity basis and rounding rule. Preserve that snapshot and calculation as decision evidence and atomically reserve the fixed amount under OD-06. Do not silently reprice an approved grant after market movements; material correction requires an authorized amendment and reservation adjustment. Define separately governed exceptions for recurring percentage instructions (each instance calculated at its designated approval event) and residual/sweep grants (amount fixed at the specified later valuation or final-settlement event). Donor-facing UI must identify whether an amount is indicative or fixed and the applicable valuation date.

validation.evidence: Required: CFO and product-owner approval of valuation snapshot definition, time zone, precision and rounding, eligible balance basis, stale price rules, capacity and reservation linkage; explicit recurring/residual exception taxonomy; accounting review of corrections; donor comprehension and adverse-market-move tests.

reviewHistory.note: User selected fixed-dollar ordinary percentage grants at approval using documented valuation snapshot, with separately defined exceptions for recurring and residual grants. Formal CFO/product approval outstanding.

questions.question: Priority among approved grants in an over-committed fund
questions.optionsOrValidation: Approval order · pro rata · sponsor discretion

decision.recommendedAnswer: Working design: allocate scarce grant-funding capacity by the sequence of valid, effective reservations, preserving existing encumbrances unless an authorized legal or compliance hold or correction requires otherwise. Exceptional grants approved pending funding have no reservation priority until a valid reservation is created; maintain them in a controlled, transparent queue with documented ordering and re-evaluation. Sponsor-authorized exceptions require documented rationale, appropriate delegation-of-authority approval, legal and accounting checks, affected-party impact review and immutable audit history. Never use queue reordering to evade enforceable recipient commitments, sanctions holds or funding restrictions. Partial funding requires separately approved sponsor policy; do not silently reduce fixed grants.

validation.evidence: Required: sponsor board approval of reservation priority and exception authority; legal/accounting review of enforceable recipient obligations and funding restrictions; concurrency-safe reservation sequence definition, queue fairness and starvation controls, revaluation/return handling, and auditability; simulation of competing reservations, capacity loss, queue reordering and partial funding.

reviewHistory.note: User selected valid reservation sequence with preservation of existing reservations, controlled pending-funding queue and sponsor-authorized documented exceptions subject to legal checks and audit history. Formal board approval pending.

questions.question: Destination and tax-reporting treatment of a recipient refund
questions.optionsOrValidation: Back to fund · sponsor general · redirect

decision.recommendedAnswer: Working design: credit recipient grant refunds to the originating DAF's accounting balance by default, not to the donor personally, subject to governing documents, fund status and restrictions, and counsel-approved exceptions. Match every refund to the original grant, payment and recipient; reconcile bank/custodian receipts and ledger entries; preserve an immutable audit trail and correct grant/payment status without deleting the original transaction. Place unmatched, disputed, partial, cross-year or post-closure refunds in a controlled suspense/case workflow pending authorized disposition. Require CFO and counsel review of recognition, tax-reporting consequences and any restrictions before final posting or redirection.

validation.evidence: Required: CFO and counsel approval of default destination, governing-document and fund-closure exceptions, restrictions, tax-year and information-return handling; bank-to-ledger reconciliation procedure; identification of partial, duplicate, unidentified and cross-year refunds; authorized suspense and correction controls; external CPA input where material.

reviewHistory.note: User selected default credit to originating DAF accounting balance, subject to governing documents, counsel-approved exceptions, accounting/tax review, reconciliation and audit. Formal CFO/counsel approvals outstanding.

questions.question: Fee vs grant priority when a fund is over-committed

decision.recommendedAnswer: Working design: recognize and accrue authorized sponsor fees before computing new grant-reservable capacity, using the approved fee schedule and accounting policy. Preserve valid existing grant reservations; fee accrual or collection must not silently consume, subordinate, or release already reserved grant capacity. Where reversals, valuation changes, fee corrections, or other events create a genuine shortfall, place affected activity under a controlled hold and require sponsor-authorized resolution with documented financial, legal and contractual review. Available remedies may include authorized fee deferral or waiver, sponsor-funded remediation, and other legally permissible adjustments; never automatically reduce a fixed approved grant or override an enforceable recipient obligation.

validation.evidence: Required: CFO approval of fee accrual timing, reservable-capacity waterfall and shortfall authority; counsel/accounting review of governing documents, enforceable grants and fee waiver or deferral treatment; controls for stale NAV, reversals, accrued-versus-collected fees, fee corrections and conflicting reservations; independent reconciliation and audit of all exceptions.

reviewHistory.note: User selected fee accrual before new grant-capacity calculation, protection of existing valid reservations and sponsor-authorized review of genuine shortfalls. No silent consumption of reserved funds; formal CFO and legal/accounting approvals pending.

questions.question: Destination of trailing receipts after closure
questions.optionsOrValidation: Successor fund · sponsor unrestricted · original grantee

decision.recommendedAnswer: Working design: classify every post-closure receipt by source and legal character (including grant refund, investment distribution, custodian correction, recovery and unidentified receipt), retain linkage to the closed DAF and original transactions, and follow governing documents plus documented closure instructions. Where legally eligible, allocate trailing receipts to the valid designated successor DAF first; otherwise apply a sponsor-board-approved charitable disposition policy, with counsel and accounting review as appropriate. Do not automatically reopen a closed DAF, redirect funds to a donor personally, or treat all receipt types as interchangeable. Use controlled suspense accounting for ambiguous, disputed or unmatched receipts; require bank/custodian reconciliation, authorized posting, tax/reporting review and immutable audit history.

validation.evidence: Required: sponsor board and counsel approval of default charitable disposition and governing-document precedence; closure/successor designation validity checks; CFO/accounting review of trailing receipt classifications, restrictions, suspense accounts and cross-period treatment; reconciliation and evidence controls for post-closure receipts, duplicate receipts, invalid successors and unidentified payments.

reviewHistory.note: User selected governing documents and closure instructions first, valid designated successor DAF for eligible trailing receipts, otherwise sponsor-approved charitable disposition, with classification, reconciliation, legal review and audit. Board/counsel approvals outstanding.

questions.question: Retention schedule per record class, and precedence over privacy deletion

decision.recommendedAnswer: Working design: maintain a counsel-approved, versioned retention and disposition schedule by record class, specifying applicable legal basis and jurisdiction, retention start/stop trigger, retention period once legally validated, access restrictions, privacy deletion eligibility, legal hold precedence, and defensible deletion or preservation procedures. Do not invent default periods. Apply policy to primary records, backups, exports, partner copies, AI context/derived artifacts and generated evidence, with practical propagation and backup-expiry controls. Honor eligible privacy deletion and minimization requests while preserving records subject to legal, regulatory, tax, accounting or litigation holds; document decisions, authority, exceptions and immutable audit evidence without retaining unnecessarily sensitive deleted content.

validation.evidence: Required: general counsel approval of record-class taxonomy, applicable jurisdictions, statutory/contractual retention periods, legal hold and privacy deletion precedence; privacy/security review of data inventories and deletion propagation to backups, vendors, AI stores and exports; operational tests for hold/release, subject access/deletion, scheduled disposition, exceptions and auditability. No numeric retention periods approved.

reviewHistory.note: User selected counsel-approved retention by record class with legal basis, jurisdiction, triggers, holds, privacy deletion eligibility, minimization and auditable disposition; no arbitrary periods until validated. Formal counsel approval pending.
